current_description.description_medium: On October 10, 2025, Melania Trump said eight children displaced by the Russia-Ukraine war had been reunited with family members after months of back-channel contacts with Russia. The Associated Press reported that the children included three displaced to Russia by front-line fighting and five separated from relatives across borders. The announcement was attributed to the first lady; the article did not independently identify the children or detail each return. The entry should preserve that attribution and avoid implying that all eight were Ukrainian children.

proposal.original_claim_summary: Trump Threatens to Court-Martial Generals Who Criticized Him

identified_problems.explanation: Repeated searches did not locate credible contemporaneous reporting that Trump publicly threatened February 2025 court-martials of retired Generals Mark Milley and James Mattis.
A documented January 2025 action concerned revoking Milley's clearance/security detail and reviewing whether his retired rank should be reduced, which is not the same as threatening a court-martial.

frozen_original.title: Trump Threatens to Court-Martial Generals Who Criticized Him
frozen_original.synopsis: In February 2025, Trump publicly threatened to seek court-martials for retired generals who had spoken critically of him, including former Chairman of the Joint Chiefs Mark Milley and former Defense Secretary James Mattis. The threats represented an extraordinary attempt to use military law to silence civilian critics who had once served in uniform. Legal experts noted that retired officers retain First Amendment rights and cannot be court-martialed for speech made after leaving service. The threats were widely condemned as an attempt to intimidate the military brass and chill any future dissent from senior officers.

proposal.original_claim_summary: Trump Ends All Federal LGBTQ+ Health Programs on Day One
proposal.original_synopsis: On January 20, 2025, Trump signed executive orders that effectively ended all federal LGBTQ+-specific health programs, including the HHS Office of Minority Health programs addressing health disparities among LGBTQ+ individuals, CDC programs tracking HIV among gay and bisexual men, mental health crisis resources specifically targeting LGBTQ+ youth at elevated suicide risk, and federally funded community health center programs serving LGBTQ+ patients. The orders directed federal agencies to cease collecting demographic data on sexual orientation and gender identity, making it impossible to track health disparities. The Trevor Project and other LGBTQ+ mental health organizations reported immediate spikes in crisis calls from LGBTQ+ youth following the executive orders, citing fear and distress over the removal of federal recognition.

proposal.original_claim_summary: Trump administration creates list of subversive academics
proposal.original_synopsis: The Trump administration compiled and circulated a list of academics deemed subversive, targeting university professors and researchers for their political views and chilling academic freedom. The list was reportedly compiled by White House staff and shared with federal agencies, university administrators, and congressional allies. Academics on the list reported increased scrutiny of their research grants, visa applications, and professional activities. The move was condemned by university presidents and civil liberties groups as McCarthyism.
